components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — money; also in 钱 money, 银 silver.
旁 (páng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 磅 bàng and 傍 bàng.

example.hanzi: 这本书卖十英镑。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū mài shí yīngbàng.
example.english: This book costs ten pounds.
example.fact: 镑 appears essentially in 英镑 (pound sterling). The weight 'pound' is written 磅, with a stone radical instead of metal.

examples.hanzi: 一英镑是多少人民币？
examples.pinyin: Yì yīngbàng shì duōshao rénmínbì?
examples.english: How many yuan is one pound?

examples.hanzi: 这件外套要五十英镑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn wàitào yào wǔshí yīngbàng.
examples.english: This coat costs fifty pounds.

components.note: 虫 (insect, creature) — small animals, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito.
下 (xià) is only a loose sound clue for xiā.

example.hanzi: 这盘虾很新鲜。
example.pinyin: Zhè pán xiā hěn xīnxiān.
example.english: This plate of shrimp is very fresh.
example.fact: 虾 is the shrimp; 龙虾 is a lobster, 小龙虾 is crayfish (a hugely popular summer street food), and 虾米 is dried shrimp.

examples.hanzi: 我最爱吃的是炒虾仁。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì ài chī de shì chǎo xiārén.
examples.english: My favorite dish is stir-fried shrimp.

examples.hanzi: 他在海边买了几斤大虾。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hǎibiān mǎi le jǐ jīn dàxiā.
examples.english: He bought a few catties of prawns by the sea.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.
彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.

example.hanzi: 这台机器需要定期维修才能正常运行。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì xūyào dìngqī wéixiū cáinéng zhèngcháng yùnxíng.
example.english: This machine needs regular maintenance to run normally.
example.fact: The Eiffel Tower requires roughly 60 tons of paint reapplied by hand every seven years as part of its maintenance routine, partly to protect the iron structure from rust.

examples.hanzi: 电梯坏了，工人正在维修。
examples.pinyin: Diàntī huài le, gōngrén zhèngzài wéixiū.
examples.english: The elevator is broken, and workers are repairing it.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车的维修费用太高了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē de wéixiū fèiyòng tài gāo le.
examples.english: The repair costs for this car are too high.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
玉 (jade) — playing with a piece of jade; also in 国 country, 宝 treasure.
廾 (two hands) — hands holding something; 弄 is to handle or play with.

example.hanzi: 他总是玩弄别人的感情，从不认真。
example.pinyin: tā zǒngshì wánnòng biérén de gǎnqíng, cóng bù rènzhēn.
example.english: He always toys with other people's feelings and is never serious about them.
example.fact: Domestic cats often keep playing with captured prey for minutes before finally killing it, batting it around even when they are not hungry. Ethologists trace this to leftover predatory instinct: the movements of stalking, pouncing, and release are partly automatic, so a cat 'practices' the full hunting sequence on anything that still moves.

examples.hanzi: 别玩弄文字游戏了，说实话吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié wánnòng wénzì yóuxì le, shuō shíhuà ba.
examples.english: Stop playing word games and tell the truth.

examples.hanzi: 小猫正在玩弄一个毛线球。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎomāo zhèngzài wánnòng yī gè máoxiàn qiú.
examples.english: The kitten is playing with a ball of yarn.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.hanzi: 这款翻译软件不光能翻译文字，还能识别语音。
example.pinyin: zhè kuǎn fānyì ruǎnjiàn bùguāng néng fānyì wénzì, hái néng shíbié yǔyīn.
example.english: This translation software can not only translate text, but also recognize speech.
example.fact: One of the earliest speech recognition systems, Bell Labs' "Audrey" from 1952, could only recognize spoken digits zero through nine, and even then only reliably for the voice of the specific engineer who trained it. Modern systems recognizing continuous speech from any speaker took several more decades of research to arrive.

examples.hanzi: 不光我一个人这么想，大家都有同感。
examples.pinyin: Bù guāng wǒ yī gè rén zhème xiǎng, dàjiā dōu yǒu tónggǎn.
examples.english: I'm not the only one who thinks so; everyone feels the same.

examples.hanzi: 她不光长得漂亮，而且心地善良。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù guāng zhǎng de piàoliang, érqiě xīndì shànliáng.
examples.english: She is not only pretty but also kind-hearted.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
子 (child) — a child in a house: to bear and nurture; characters were later "born" from other characters.

example.hanzi: 楔形文字是世界上最古老的文字之一。
example.pinyin: xiēxíng wénzì shì shìjiè shàng zuì gǔlǎo de wénzì zhī yī.
example.english: Cuneiform is one of the oldest writing systems in the world.
example.fact: Cuneiform was developed in Sumer, in what is now southern Iraq, around 3400 BCE, initially to keep track of grain shipments and temple accounts. Scribes pressed wedge-shaped marks into wet clay tablets with a reed stylus, and thousands of these tablets have survived to the present day simply because the clay hardened over millennia.

examples.hanzi: 这本书的文字很简单，适合初学者。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de wénzì hěn jiǎndān, shìhé chūxuézhě.
examples.english: The writing in this book is simple and suitable for beginners.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用文字或者图片来表达想法。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng wénzì huòzhě túpiàn lái biǎodá xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: You can express your ideas with words or pictures.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
阝 (town, from 邑) on the right — marks places and towns, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 邻 neighbour.
良 (liáng) hints at the sound: 郎 láng is close, as in 狼 láng, 廊 láng and 朗 lǎng.

example.hanzi: 新郎在婚礼上向新娘许下了誓言。
example.pinyin: xīnláng zài hūnlǐ shàng xiàng xīnniáng xǔxiàle shìyán.
example.english: The groom made his vows to the bride at the wedding.
example.fact: The modern custom of giving a diamond engagement ring owes much to a 1947 De Beers advertising campaign built around the slogan "A Diamond Is Forever." Before that campaign, diamond rings were far less standard as a wedding tradition in much of the West.

examples.hanzi: 新郎穿着黑色的西装，显得很精神。
examples.pinyin: Xīnláng chuān zhe hēisè de xīzhuāng, xiǎnde hěn jīngshen.
examples.english: The groom wore a black suit and looked sharp.

examples.hanzi: 新郎和新娘一起给客人敬酒。
examples.pinyin: Xīnláng hé xīnniáng yīqǐ gěi kèrén jìngjiǔ.
examples.english: The bride and groom proposed toasts to the guests together.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 科学家很难预见十年后的天气变化。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā hěn nán yùjiàn shí nián hòu de tiānqì biànhuà.
example.english: Scientists find it hard to foresee weather changes ten years from now.
example.fact: In 1922, mathematician Lewis Fry Richardson attempted the first numerical weather forecast by hand, spending roughly six weeks of calculation to predict just six hours of future weather — and his result turned out to be wildly inaccurate. Today's supercomputers run similar equations, refined over a century, to produce forecasts in minutes.

examples.hanzi: 好的领导能预见到未来的困难。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo de lǐngdǎo néng yùjiàn dào wèilái de kùnnan.
examples.english: A good leader can foresee future difficulties.

examples.hanzi: 谁也没有预见到这场危机会来得这么快。
examples.pinyin: Shéi yě méiyǒu yùjiàn dào zhè chǎng wēijī huì lái de zhème kuài.
examples.english: No one foresaw that this crisis would arrive so quickly.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — the top. 姜 is the Jiang clan name; the 'ginger' meaning (生姜) is borrowed from the old 薑. Memory aid: sheep and ginger go well together.
女 (woman) — many ancient clan names carry it: 姓 surname, 姬, 姚. Here it marks 姜 as a clan name, not female meaning.

example.hanzi: 做鱼的时候要放一点姜。
example.pinyin: Zuò yú de shíhou yào fàng yìdiǎn jiāng.
example.english: When cooking fish you need to add a little ginger.
example.fact: 姜 is also a common surname. The proverb 姜还是老的辣 ('old ginger is the spiciest') means experience beats youth.

examples.hanzi: 煮鱼汤时，我会放几片姜。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔ yútāng shí, wǒ huì fàng jǐ piàn jiāng.
examples.english: When I cook fish soup, I add a few slices of ginger.

examples.hanzi: 冬天喝一杯姜茶很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān hē yì bēi jiāngchá hěn shūfu.
examples.english: A cup of ginger tea is comforting in winter.

components.note: 亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.
亻 (person) — person radical — 伦 is about human relations and order, 伦理 ethics.
仑 (lún) — same sound — 仑 also sounds out 轮 lún and 论 lùn.

example.hanzi: 亚伦是瑙鲁的首都。
example.pinyin: Yàlún shì Nàolǔ de shǒudū.
example.english: Yaren is the capital of Nauru.
example.fact: Nauru is the world's third-smallest country by area, at just under 21 square kilometers, and it has no official capital city — Yaren is simply the district that hosts most government buildings. The island was once wealthy from phosphate mining, but decades of extraction stripped much of its interior down to bare coral rock.

examples.hanzi: 亚伦是我大学时最好的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Yàlún shì wǒ dàxué shí zuì hǎo de péngyou.
examples.english: Aaron was my best friend in college.

examples.hanzi: 你认识那个叫亚伦的美国学生吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi nàge jiào Yàlún de Měiguó xuésheng ma?
examples.english: Do you know the American student named Aaron?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.

example.hanzi: 客人进屋前先脱了鞋。
example.pinyin: kèrén jìn wū qián xiān tuōle xié.
example.english: The guest took off his shoes before entering the room.
example.fact: In traditional Japanese homes, the genkan is a sunken entryway where visitors remove their shoes before stepping up onto the raised floor of the house proper. The height difference is not just decorative — it physically marks the boundary between the outside world and the clean, often tatami-matted, living space.

examples.hanzi: 外面太冷了，快进屋吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài lěng le, kuài jìnwū ba.
examples.english: It's too cold out there, so come inside quickly.

examples.hanzi: 他一进屋就打开了灯。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī jìnwū jiù dǎkāi le dēng.
examples.english: As soon as he entered the room, he turned on the light.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 职 is the duty one hears and remembers.
只 (zhī) is a near sound match for zhí; also in 织 zhī and 识 shí.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 这家公司的职员每天早上八点上班。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī de zhíyuán měitiān zǎoshang bā diǎn shàngbān.
example.english: The staff at this company start work at eight every morning.
example.fact: Designer Robert Propst created the "Action Office" system in 1968, intending to give office staff more privacy and flexibility than open desks allowed. The idea was later simplified and mass-produced by manufacturers into the smaller, denser cubicle grids that came to define office work for decades — the opposite of what Propst had originally envisioned.

examples.hanzi: 银行的职员热情地帮我办了手续。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng de zhíyuán rèqíng de bāng wǒ bàn le shǒuxù.
examples.english: The bank clerk kindly helped me with the paperwork.

examples.hanzi: 公司新招了五名职员。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xīn zhāo le wǔ míng zhíyuán.
examples.english: The company has hired five new staff members.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
齿 (teeth) — 齿 is the tooth radical — age was read from teeth, as in 年龄.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 龄 is líng; 令 also sounds out 领 lǐng and 铃 líng.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 我们周末常常去打保龄球。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōumò chángcháng qù dǎ bǎolíngqiú.
example.english: We often go bowling on weekends.
example.fact: British archaeologist Sir Flinders Petrie excavated pins and balls resembling bowling equipment from an Egyptian child's grave dating to roughly 3200 BCE, suggesting some form of the game may be over 5,000 years old. The oldest confirmed indoor bowling lane, however, dates only to 14th-century Germany.

examples.hanzi: 周末我和朋友去打了两局保龄球。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ hé péngyou qù dǎ le liǎng jú bǎolíngqiú.
examples.english: On the weekend, my friends and I played two rounds of bowling.

examples.hanzi: 他一个保龄球就打出了全中。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī gè bǎolíngqiú jiù dǎ chū le quánzhòng.
examples.english: He rolled a strike with a single bowling ball.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and weaving, as in 线, 红, 绳; 编 is to weave, then to compile.
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound: 编 biān is close, as in 偏 piān and 篇 piān.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的编剧曾获得奥斯卡奖。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de biānjù céng huòdé Àosīkǎ jiǎng.
example.english: The screenwriter of this film once won an Oscar.
example.fact: At the very first Academy Awards ceremony in 1929, writing was honored with two separate awards — one for original story and one for adapted screenplay — a split that reflected how young and unsettled the craft of film screenwriting still was in Hollywood's early sound era.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位很有才华的年轻编剧。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi hěn yǒu cáihuá de niánqīng biānjù.
examples.english: He is a very talented young screenwriter.

examples.hanzi: 编剧花了半年时间才写完这个剧本。
examples.pinyin: Biānjù huā le bàn nián shíjiān cái xiě wán zhège jùběn.
examples.english: The screenwriter took half a year to finish this script.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.
匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.

example.hanzi: 这条地铁线路直达市区中心。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo dìtiě xiànlù zhídá shìqū zhōngxīn.
example.english: This subway line goes straight to the city center.
example.fact: According to a 2007 United Nations estimate, humanity crossed a historic threshold that year: for the first time, more than half of the world's population lived in urban districts rather than rural areas. UN projections suggest that share will keep climbing through the rest of the century.

examples.hanzi: 从机场到市区大约要四十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Cóng jīchǎng dào shìqū dàyuē yào sìshí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: It takes about forty minutes from the airport to downtown.

examples.hanzi: 市区里的房价比郊区贵得多。
examples.pinyin: Shìqū lǐ de fángjià bǐ jiāoqū guì de duō.
examples.english: Housing prices downtown are much higher than in the suburbs.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.
目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.

example.hanzi: 参加会议的人数目不算多。
example.pinyin: cānjiā huìyì de rén shùmù bú suàn duō.
example.english: The number of people attending the meeting isn't very large.
example.fact: Zero as a true number, not just an empty placeholder, was given formal mathematical rules by Indian mathematician Brahmagupta around 628 CE, including rules for adding, subtracting, and multiplying with zero and negative numbers — ideas that took centuries longer to reach and be accepted in Europe.

examples.hanzi: 这笔钱的数目不小，你要小心保管。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ qián de shùmù bù xiǎo, nǐ yào xiǎoxīn bǎoguǎn.
examples.english: This is not a small sum of money, so keep it carefully.

examples.hanzi: 请你核对一下账单上的数目。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ héduì yīxià zhàngdān shàng de shùmù.
examples.english: Please check the amount on the bill.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words, as in 说 say, 话 speech; 诗 is spoken verse.
寺 (sì) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 时 shí, 持 chí and 特 tè.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这位诗人写下了许多描写自然的诗篇。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi shīrén xiěxiàle xǔduō miáoxiě zìrán de shīpiān.
example.english: This poet wrote many poems describing nature.
example.fact: The Epic of Gilgamesh, composed in Mesopotamia more than 4,000 years ago, is widely considered the oldest surviving major work of literature, predating Homer's Iliad and Odyssey by well over a thousand years.

examples.hanzi: 李白是中国唐代最有名的诗人。
examples.pinyin: Lǐ Bái shì Zhōngguó Tángdài zuì yǒumíng de shīrén.
examples.english: Li Bai is the most famous poet of China's Tang dynasty.

examples.hanzi: 这位年轻的诗人刚出版了第一本诗集。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi niánqīng de shīrén gāng chūbǎn le dì yī běn shījí.
examples.english: This young poet has just published his first poetry collection.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国 country, 回 return, 图 map; 园 is a fenced garden.
元 (yuán) sounds exactly like 园; also in 远 yuǎn, 院 yuàn, 完 wán.

example.hanzi: 洪水过后，村民们努力重建家园。
example.pinyin: hóngshuǐ guòhòu, cūnmínmen nǔlì chóngjiàn jiāyuán.
example.english: After the flood, the villagers worked hard to rebuild their homes.
example.fact: Arctic terns migrate roughly 70,000 kilometers round trip each year between Arctic breeding grounds and Antarctic waters — the longest known migration of any animal — and individual birds have been tracked returning to the very same nesting site year after year.

examples.hanzi: 我们要保护地球，这是人类共同的家园。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎohù dìqiú, zhè shì rénlèi gòngtóng de jiāyuán.
examples.english: We must protect the Earth, our shared home.

examples.hanzi: 战争让许多人失去了家园。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng ràng xǔduō rén shīqù le jiāyuán.
examples.english: The war made many people lose their homes.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
九 — originally a bent arm (elbow), later borrowed to write nine. 九 also sounds out 究 jiū and 鸠 jiū.

example.hanzi: 贝多芬的第九交响曲是他最后一部完整的交响作品。
example.pinyin: Bèiduōfēn de dìjiǔ jiāoxiǎngqǔ shì tā zuìhòu yī bù wánzhěng de jiāoxiǎng zuòpǐn.
example.english: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is his last complete symphonic work.
example.fact: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony while almost completely deaf. At its 1824 premiere, he stood on stage helping conduct, but a fellow musician reportedly had to turn him around to face the audience so he could see, rather than hear, them applauding.

examples.hanzi: 我住在这栋楼的第九层。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài zhè dòng lóu de dìjiǔ céng.
examples.english: I live on the ninth floor of this building.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中得了第九名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng dé le dì jiǔ míng.
examples.english: He came ninth in the competition.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 新工厂下个月正式开工。
example.pinyin: xīn gōngchǎng xià gè yuè zhèngshì kāigōng.
example.english: The new factory will formally start operations next month.
example.fact: Construction on the Hoover Dam began in 1931 and finished more than two years ahead of schedule, using enough concrete — about 3.3 million cubic meters — that engineers at the time calculated it could pave a two-lane highway stretching from San Francisco to New York.

examples.hanzi: 工人们早上六点就开工了。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zǎoshang liù diǎn jiù kāigōng le.
examples.english: The workers started work at six in the morning.

examples.hanzi: 过完年，工厂大年初八开工。
examples.pinyin: Guò wán nián, gōngchǎng dà nián chū bā kāigōng.
examples.english: After the New Year holiday, the factory resumes work on the eighth day.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — 鱼 is the fish radical, as in 鲨, 鲸; 鲜 pairs 鱼 with 羊 (sheep) — both freshly tasty foods, so fresh.
皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.

example.hanzi: 医生用纱布止住了伤口流出的鲜血。
example.pinyin: yīshēng yòng shābù zhǐzhùle shāngkǒu liúchū de xiānxuè.
example.english: The doctor used gauze to stop the fresh blood flowing from the wound.
example.fact: An average adult human body holds about 5 liters of blood, and its red color comes from hemoglobin, an iron-containing protein in red blood cells that binds oxygen in the lungs and carries it out to the rest of the body.

examples.hanzi: 战士的鲜血染红了战旗。
examples.pinyin: Zhànshì de xiānxuè rǎn hóng le zhànqí.
examples.english: The soldier's blood stained the flag red.

examples.hanzi: 医生看到他满手鲜血，立刻开始急救。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng kàndào tā mǎn shǒu xiānxuè, lìkè kāishǐ jíjiù.
examples.english: The doctor saw his hands covered in blood and began first aid immediately.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — money; also in 钱 money, 银 silver.
旁 (páng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 磅 bàng and 傍 bàng.

example.hanzi: 这件外套的价格是五十英镑。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn wàitào de jiàgé shì wǔshí Yīngbàng.
example.english: This coat costs fifty pounds.
example.fact: The British pound sterling, first issued around the 8th century, is widely regarded as the oldest currency still in continuous use anywhere in the world today.

examples.hanzi: 一英镑等于多少人民币？
examples.pinyin: Yī yīngbàng děngyú duōshao rénmínbì?
examples.english: How many yuan is one pound worth?

examples.hanzi: 我在伦敦换了两百英镑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Lúndūn huàn le liǎng bǎi yīngbàng.
examples.english: I exchanged two hundred pounds in London.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院, 队; hiding behind a mound — 隐 is to conceal; the right side is a simplified stand-in.
彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.

example.hanzi: F-117是世界上第一种投入实战的隐形战斗机。
example.pinyin: F-117 shì shìjiè shàng dì yī zhǒng tóurù shízhàn de yǐnxíng zhàndòujī.
example.english: The F-117 was the world's first stealth fighter used in actual combat.
example.fact: The F-117 Nighthawk, unveiled publicly in 1988, achieved its radar-evading stealth mainly through flat, angular panels that scatter incoming radar waves away from their source, rather than through any exotic radar-absorbing material as its main trick.

examples.hanzi: 我戴隐形眼镜已经三年了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dài yǐnxíng yǎnjìng yǐjīng sān nián le.
examples.english: I've worn contact lenses for three years now.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的魔法斗篷能让人隐形。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de mófǎ dǒupeng néng ràng rén yǐnxíng.
examples.english: The magic cloak in the story can make a person invisible.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 召 itself sounds out 招 zhāo, 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
刀 (dāo) is only a loose sound clue for zhào.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.

example.hanzi: 校长召集了全体老师开紧急会议。
example.pinyin: xiàozhǎng zhàojíle quántǐ lǎoshī kāi jǐnjí huìyì.
example.english: The principal convened all the teachers for an emergency meeting.
example.fact: The first General Assembly of the United Nations was convened in London in January 1946, bringing together representatives of the 51 founding member states less than a year after the end of the Second World War.

examples.hanzi: 班长召集同学们开了个会。
examples.pinyin: Bānzhǎng zhàojí tóngxuémen kāi le gè huì.
examples.english: The class monitor called the students together for a meeting.

examples.hanzi: 他召集了几个朋友来帮忙搬家。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhàojí le jǐ gè péngyou lái bāngmáng bānjiā.
examples.english: He gathered a few friends to help him move.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower and 草 grass; it points to crops and harvest, the sense in 收获. Simplified 获 replaces 獲's left side with 艹.
犾 (dog-like part) — a variant of 犬 dog; 獲 originally meant catching game. Memory aid: grass plus a hunting dog, you bring something home.
耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.

example.hanzi: 章鱼能瞬间获取周围环境的颜色和纹理。
example.pinyin: zhāngyú néng shùnjiān huòqǔ zhōuwéi huánjìng de yánsè hé wénlǐ.
example.english: Octopuses can instantly acquire the colors and textures of their surroundings.
example.fact: Octopus skin holds thousands of pigment-filled cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by the nervous system, which let an octopus shift its camouflage pattern in a fraction of a second — far faster than any manufactured color-changing material yet built.

examples.hanzi: 你可以在网上免费获取这些资料。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngshàng miǎnfèi huòqǔ zhèxiē zīliào.
examples.english: You can get this material online for free.

examples.hanzi: 多读书是获取知识的好办法。
examples.pinyin: Duō dúshū shì huòqǔ zhīshi de hǎo bànfǎ.
examples.english: Reading more is a good way to acquire knowledge.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the bottom part, the meat/body radical as in 脑, 脚, 胖. Early forms show meat on a bone, but that does not explain 'willing' today.
止 (stop, foot) — the top. Dictionary story: stop 止 flexing muscle ⺼. Memory aid: you stop resisting and agree — 肯定, a hedged mnemonic.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 过 pass, 进 enter.

example.hanzi: 肯尼迪是美国历史上最年轻的当选总统。
example.pinyin: Kěnnídí shì Měiguó lìshǐ shàng zuì niánqīng de dāngxuǎn zǒngtǒng.
example.english: Kennedy was the youngest elected president in American history.
example.fact: John F. Kennedy was 43 years old when he took office in January 1961, making him the youngest person ever elected U.S. president — Theodore Roosevelt was younger when he became president, but he did so through succession after an assassination, not through an election.

examples.hanzi: 肯尼迪机场是纽约最繁忙的机场之一。
examples.pinyin: Kěnnídí jīchǎng shì Niǔyuē zuì fánmáng de jīchǎng zhī yī.
examples.english: Kennedy Airport is one of the busiest airports in New York.

examples.hanzi: 历史课上，老师讲到了肯尼迪总统。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐ kè shàng, lǎoshī jiǎng dào le Kěnnídí zǒngtǒng.
examples.english: In history class, the teacher talked about President Kennedy.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — spoken orders; also in 叫 shout, 说 speak.
分 (fēn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 纷 fēn, 芬 fēn and 粉 fěn.
口 (mouth) — spoken instructions; also in 叫 shout, 问 ask.
付 (fù) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 附 fù.

example.hanzi: 妈妈吩咐我放学后去买菜。
example.pinyin: māma fēnfu wǒ fàngxué hòu qù mǎi cài.
example.english: Mom instructed me to go buy groceries after school.
example.fact: Leafcutter ants communicate almost entirely through chemical pheromone trails rather than sound, effectively instructing thousands of nestmates on which leaves to harvest and which paths back to the colony to follow, all without a single vocal signal.

examples.hanzi: 老板吩咐秘书订两张机票。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn fēnfu mìshū dìng liǎng zhāng jīpiào.
examples.english: The boss told his secretary to book two plane tickets.

examples.hanzi: 有什么事尽管吩咐，我马上去做。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shénme shì jǐnguǎn fēnfu, wǒ mǎshàng qù zuò.
examples.english: Just tell me if you need anything, and I'll do it right away.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 沙漠的气候对旅行者非常无情。
example.pinyin: shāmò de qìhòu duì lǚxíngzhě fēicháng wúqíng.
example.english: The desert climate is utterly merciless to travelers.
example.fact: The Sahara can swing from daytime highs above 45°C to near-freezing nights, because dry sand and air release the heat they absorb almost as quickly as they take it in, leaving no gradual buffer for anyone caught crossing it after dark.

examples.hanzi: 时间是无情的，青春一去不复返。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān shì wúqíng de, qīngchūn yī qù bù fù fǎn.
examples.english: Time is merciless, and youth never returns.

examples.hanzi: 他无情地拒绝了朋友的请求。
examples.pinyin: Tā wúqíng de jùjué le péngyou de qǐngqiú.
examples.english: He coldly turned down his friend's request.

components.note: 童 (child) — as a sound unit, 童 also appears in 瞳 tóng and 撞 zhuàng; the character itself means child, as in 儿童.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 格林兄弟收集并出版了许多经典童话。
example.pinyin: Gélín xiōngdì shōují bìng chūbǎnle xǔduō jīngdiǎn tónghuà.
example.english: The Brothers Grimm collected and published many classic fairy tales.
example.fact: The Brothers Grimm first published their collection of German folk tales in 1812. Many of the stories were originally far darker and more violent than the softened versions widely told to children today; later editions were repeatedly revised to tone down the content.

examples.hanzi: 妹妹睡前总要听一个童话故事。
examples.pinyin: Mèimei shuìqián zǒng yào tīng yī gè tónghuà gùshi.
examples.english: My little sister always listens to a fairy tale before bed.

examples.hanzi: 这座城堡看起来就像童话里的一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngbǎo kàn qǐlái jiù xiàng tónghuà lǐ de yīyàng.
examples.english: This castle looks like something out of a fairy tale.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 别急，总会有法子解决这个问题的。
example.pinyin: bié jí, zǒng huì yǒu fǎzi jiějué zhège wèntí de.
example.english: Don't worry, there will always be a way to solve this problem.
example.fact: Francis Bacon's 1620 work Novum Organum helped formalize what became known as the modern scientific method, arguing that reliable knowledge should be built up from systematic observation and experiment rather than from received authority or pure abstract reasoning alone.

examples.hanzi: 你有什么好法子让孩子早点睡觉？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme hǎo fǎzi ràng háizi zǎodiǎn shuìjiào?
examples.english: Do you have any good way to get the kids to bed early?

examples.hanzi: 我实在没法子了，只好向你求助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shízài méi fǎzi le, zhǐhǎo xiàng nǐ qiúzhù.
examples.english: I really have no way out, so I have to ask you for help.

components.note: 女 (woman) — female kin and women: 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 妹 younger sister, 娘; 姑 is a father's sister.

女 (woman) — women and family, as in 她, 姐, 奶; 妈 is mother.
马 (mǎ) is a close sound clue for mā; also in 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 我的姑妈每年寒假都会来看我们。
example.pinyin: wǒ de gūmā měinián hánjià dōu huì lái kàn wǒmen.
example.english: My paternal aunt comes to visit us every winter break.
example.fact: In African elephant herds, related females — including aunts — often take turns helping care for calves that are not their own, a behavior biologists call allomothering. It helps calves survive when their own mothers are off foraging or resting.

examples.hanzi: 姑妈送了我一本很漂亮的日记本。
examples.pinyin: Gūmā sòng le wǒ yī běn hěn piàoliang de rìjìběn.
examples.english: My aunt gave me a very pretty diary.

examples.hanzi: 我和姑妈一起去市场买了菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé gūmā yīqǐ qù shìchǎng mǎi le cài.
examples.english: I went to the market with my aunt to buy vegetables.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.

example.hanzi: 数千名市民在广场举行了集会。
example.pinyin: shùqiān míng shìmín zài guǎngchǎng jǔxíngle jíhuì.
example.english: Thousands of citizens held an assembly in the square.
example.fact: Desert locusts normally live solitary lives, but when their population density rises, a spike in the neurotransmitter serotonin triggers a dramatic behavior change, driving them to swarm together into the massive gathering swarms responsible for historic crop devastation.

examples.hanzi: 学校明天早上有一个全校集会。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào míngtiān zǎoshang yǒu yī gè quánxiào jíhuì.
examples.english: The school has an assembly tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 全家人在大树下集会，庆祝节日。
examples.pinyin: Quán jiā rén zài dà shù xià jíhuì, qìngzhù jiérì.
examples.english: The whole family gathered under the big tree to celebrate the holiday.

example.hanzi: 没有做好准备，比赛的下场可想而知。

example.english: Without proper preparation, the outcome of the match was predictable.
example.fact: The phrase "the show must go on" is often traced to 19th-century circuses, where performances continued despite injuries, animal escapes, or even fires, since stopping abruptly risked panicking the audience or losing that night's ticket revenue.

examples.hanzi: 这个球员受伤后只好下场休息。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qiúyuán shòushāng hòu zhǐhǎo xiàchǎng xiūxi.
examples.english: This player had to leave the field to rest after getting injured.

examples.hanzi: 考生交卷后就可以下场了。

examples.english: Examinees may leave the exam room after handing in their papers.

example.fact: Earth's tectonic plates drift at roughly the same rate that fingernails grow, about 2 to 5 centimeters per year, yet over tens of millions of years this slow, gradual creep has assembled and broken apart entire continents.

examples.hanzi: 孩子渐渐长大，开始有自己的想法。
examples.pinyin: Háizi jiànjiàn zhǎngdà, kāishǐ yǒu zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: As the child gradually grows up, he begins to have his own ideas.

examples.hanzi: 雨渐渐小了，我们可以出门了。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ jiànjiàn xiǎo le, wǒmen kěyǐ chūmén le.
examples.english: The rain is gradually easing, so we can go out.

components.note: 丫 — a picture of a fork or branching twig, hence anything forked.

example.hanzi: 这个丫头从小就很懂事。
example.pinyin: zhège yātou cóngxiǎo jiù hěn dǒngshì.
example.english: This girl has been very sensible since she was little.
example.fact: In Victorian-era Britain, domestic service was the single largest category of employment for women, with well over a million working as maids, cooks, or nannies in private households by the late 1800s.

examples.hanzi: 丫头，快来吃饭了！

examples.english: Girl, come eat now!

examples.hanzi: 这个小丫头聪明得很，什么都会。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo yātou cōngmíng de hěn, shénme dōu huì.
examples.english: This little girl is very smart and can do everything.

example.hanzi: 我家的旧电视机终于坏了。

example.english: My family's old television set finally broke.
example.fact: Scottish engineer John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television system in 1926, transmitting a moving image of a ventriloquist's dummy using a spinning mechanical scanning disc rather than any electronic camera sensor.

examples.hanzi: 电视机的声音太大了，调小一点。
examples.pinyin: Diànshìjī de shēngyīn tài dà le, tiáo xiǎo yīdiǎn.

example.english: Apollo 11 was the first crewed mission to land on the Moon.
example.fact: The leading scientific theory holds that the Moon formed about 4.5 billion years ago when a Mars-sized body, sometimes called Theia, collided with the young Earth, flinging debris into orbit that gradually clumped together into the Moon.

examples.hanzi: 月球围绕着地球转动。
examples.pinyin: Yuèqiú wéirào zhe dìqiú zhuàndòng.

examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā jìhuà zài yuèqiú shàng jiànlì yī gè yánjiū jīdì.
examples.english: Scientists plan to build a research base on the moon.

meanings: to get out of the way

components.note: 门 (gate) — marks gates and doors, as in 问, 间, 开; 闪 is a person 人 glimpsed through a gate: a flash, to dodge.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 他大喊一声"闪开"，人群立刻让出了一条路。
example.pinyin: tā dà hǎn yī shēng "shǎnkāi", rénqún lìkè ràng chū le yī tiáo lù.
example.english: He shouted "get out of the way" and the crowd immediately made way.
example.fact: The average human visual reaction time — from seeing a sudden stimulus to physically reacting — is around 200 to 250 milliseconds, which is one reason a shouted warning can reach and move a crowd faster than everyone's eyes could otherwise spot the danger.

examples.hanzi: 快闪开，车来了！
examples.pinyin: Kuài shǎnkāi, chē lái le!
examples.english: Get out of the way, a car is coming!

examples.hanzi: 救护车一响，所有的车辆都闪开了。
examples.pinyin: Jiùhùchē yī xiǎng, suǒyǒu de chēliàng dōu shǎnkāi le.
examples.english: When the ambulance sounded, all the vehicles pulled aside.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.

example.hanzi: 家里的老二从小就比较独立。
example.pinyin: jiā lǐ de lǎo'èr cóngxiǎo jiù bǐjiào dúlì.
example.english: The second-eldest child in the family has been fairly independent since childhood.
example.fact: China's one-child policy, enforced nationwide from 1980 to 2015, dramatically reshaped family structures for decades, meaning an entire generation of Chinese children grew up largely without an older or younger sibling.

examples.hanzi: 我是家里的老二，上面有个姐姐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì jiā lǐ de lǎo'èr, shàngmiàn yǒu gè jiějie.
examples.english: I'm the second child in the family, and I have an older sister.

examples.hanzi: 老二今年刚上小学。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo'èr jīnnián gāng shàng xiǎoxué.
examples.english: The second child just started elementary school this year.

components.note: 豕 (pig) — 豕 is a pig, as in 象; 豪 was a bristly boar, then a hero; 高 gives the near sound (also in 毫 háo).

example.hanzi: 我为我的国家感到自豪。
example.pinyin: Wǒ wèi wǒ de guójiā gǎndào zìháo.
example.english: I feel proud of my country.
example.fact: 豪 is found in 自豪 (proud), 豪华 (luxurious), 豪爽 (hearty and open) and 豪言壮语 (grand words). 土豪 (rich, showy person) became a joke term in the 2010s.

examples.hanzi: 看到他的成绩，爸爸很自豪。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào tā de chéngjì, bàba hěn zìháo.
examples.english: Seeing his grades, his father was very proud.

examples.hanzi: 他住在一栋豪华的别墅里。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yí dòng háohuá de biéshù lǐ.
examples.english: He lives in a luxurious villa.

components.note: 尚 (shàng) — 尚 itself gives the sound shàng to 赏 shǎng, 掌 zhǎng and 常 cháng.

example.hanzi: 事情尚未结束。
example.pinyin: Shìqing shàng wèi jiéshù.
example.english: The matter is not yet over.
example.fact: 尚 is literary. 尚未 means 'not yet' (formal, often in news), 时尚 is 'fashion' and 高尚 is 'noble'. 和尚 (Buddhist monk) is read héshang with a neutral tone.

examples.hanzi: 新产品尚未上市。
examples.pinyin: Xīn chǎnpǐn shàng wèi shàngshì.
examples.english: The new product has not yet gone on the market.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题尚需进一步研究。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí shàng xū jìnyíbù yánjiū.
examples.english: This problem still needs further study.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 请把贵重物品交给前台保管。
example.pinyin: qǐng bǎ guìzhòng wùpǐn jiāo gěi qiántái bǎoguǎn.
example.english: Please hand over your valuables to the front desk for safekeeping.
example.fact: Fort Knox, the U.S. Bullion Depository in Kentucky, has held a large share of America's gold reserves since 1937, protected by thick granite walls and a vault door reported to weigh more than 20 tons.

examples.hanzi: 这把钥匙请你好好保管。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yàoshi qǐng nǐ hǎohāo bǎoguǎn.
examples.english: Please keep this key safe.

examples.hanzi: 放心吧，保管不会出问题。
examples.pinyin: Fàngxīn ba, bǎoguǎn bù huì chū wèntí.
examples.english: Don't worry, I guarantee nothing will go wrong.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 他找了个借口，终于从这场麻烦中脱身了。
example.pinyin: tā zhǎole gè jièkǒu, zhōngyú cóng zhè chǎng máfan zhōng tuōshēn le.
example.english: He found an excuse and finally managed to get away from the trouble.
example.fact: Octopuses can squeeze their entire soft body through any gap larger than their eyeball, since the only rigid part of their anatomy is that eyeball itself — letting them escape from enclosures that seem far too small to have ever held them.

examples.hanzi: 我现在忙得无法脱身。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài máng de wúfǎ tuōshēn.
examples.english: I'm so busy right now that I can't get away.

examples.hanzi: 他想尽办法才从那场应酬中脱身。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng jìn bànfǎ cái cóng nà chǎng yìngchou zhōng tuōshēn.
examples.english: He tried every way to get out of that social obligation.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路; 踪 is a footprint or trace.
宗 (zōng) sounds exactly like 踪; also in 综 zōng and 棕 zōng.

example.hanzi: 警方一直没能查明嫌疑人的行踪。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng yīzhí méi néng chámíng xiányírén de xíngzōng.
example.english: The police were never able to determine the suspect's whereabouts.
example.fact: The Global Positioning System, first launched by the U.S. Department of Defense in 1978, now relies on a constellation of at least 24 satellites orbiting roughly 20,200 kilometers above Earth to pinpoint a receiver's location almost anywhere on the planet.

examples.hanzi: 他的行踪很神秘，没有人知道他去了哪里。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xíngzōng hěn shénmì, méiyǒu rén zhīdào tā qù le nǎlǐ.
examples.english: His whereabouts are mysterious, and nobody knows where he went.

examples.hanzi: 记者一路追踪，发现了明星的行踪。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě yīlù zhuīzōng, fāxiàn le míngxīng de xíngzōng.
examples.english: The reporter followed all the way and discovered the star's whereabouts.

components.note: 孚 (a hand over a child) — the usual reading is a mother nursing her child, hence breast and milk.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 医生建议她定期做乳房检查。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì tā dìngqī zuò rǔfáng jiǎnchá.
example.english: The doctor advised her to have regular breast examinations.
example.fact: Breast milk composition changes not only from mother to mother but even during a single feeding, typically starting out thinner and more watery and gradually becoming richer in fat as the feeding goes on.

examples.hanzi: 医生说乳房定期检查很重要。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō rǔfáng dìngqī jiǎnchá hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: The doctor said regular breast checkups are important.

examples.hanzi: 母牛的乳房需要每天清洁。
examples.pinyin: Mǔniú de rǔfáng xūyào měitiān qīngjié.
examples.english: A cow's udder needs to be cleaned every day.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and language, as in 说 say, 请 please, 谢 thank.
斥 (chì) is only a loose sound hint for sù.

example.hanzi: 被告决定向上一级法院提出上诉。
example.pinyin: bèigào juédìng xiàng shàng yī jí fǎyuàn tíchū shàngsù.
example.english: The defendant decided to file an appeal with the higher court.
example.fact: The U.S. Supreme Court, established in 1789, hears only a tiny fraction of the roughly 7,000 to 8,000 appeal petitions filed each year, typically agreeing to fully review fewer than 100 to 150 of them.

examples.hanzi: 如果你不同意判决，可以上诉。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ bù tóngyì pànjué, kěyǐ shàngsù.
examples.english: If you disagree with the verdict, you can appeal.

examples.hanzi: 他的上诉最后被法院驳回了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shàngsù zuìhòu bèi fǎyuàn bóhuí le.
examples.english: His appeal was finally rejected by the court.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.
弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 地球的吸引力使我们的双脚稳稳地站在地面上。
example.pinyin: dìqiú de xīyǐnlì shǐ wǒmen de shuāng jiǎo wěnwěn de zhàn zài dìmiàn shàng.
example.english: Earth's gravitational pull keeps our feet firmly planted on the ground.
example.fact: Isaac Newton published his law of universal gravitation in 1687, showing that the same force pulling an apple to the ground also keeps the Moon in orbit around Earth — one of the first times a single law was shown to govern both earthly and celestial motion.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市对年轻人有很大的吸引力。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì duì niánqīngrén yǒu hěn dà de xīyǐnlì.
examples.english: This city has great appeal for young people.

examples.hanzi: 广告需要有足够的吸引力才能让人注意。
examples.pinyin: Guǎnggào xūyào yǒu zúgòu de xīyǐnlì cái néng ràng rén zhùyì.
examples.english: An advertisement needs enough appeal to catch people's attention.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
尚 (shàng) — 尚 itself gives the sound shàng to 赏 shǎng, 掌 zhǎng and 常 cháng.

example.hanzi: 他一直以高尚的品德受到大家的尊重。
example.pinyin: tā yīzhí yǐ gāoshàng de pǐndé shòudào dàjiā de zūnzhòng.
example.english: He has always been respected by everyone for his noble character.
example.fact: Mount Everest, standing 8,849 meters above sea level, grows a few millimeters taller most years as the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates continue to collide and slowly push the Himalayas upward.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个品格高尚的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī gè pǐngé gāoshàng de rén.
examples.english: He is a person of noble character.

examples.hanzi: 帮助别人是一种高尚的行为。
examples.pinyin: Bāngzhù biérén shì yī zhǒng gāoshàng de xíngwéi.
examples.english: Helping others is a noble act.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.hanzi: 房间里的光线太暗，看不清书上的字。
example.pinyin: fángjiān lǐ de guāngxiàn tài àn, kàn bù qīng shū shàng de zì.
example.english: The light in the room is too dim to read the words in the book clearly.
example.fact: Light travels at about 299,792 kilometers per second in a vacuum, a speed first estimated with reasonable accuracy in 1676 by Danish astronomer Ole Rømer, who noticed delays in the timing of eclipses of Jupiter's moons depending on Earth's distance from Jupiter.

examples.hanzi: 这间屋子光线很好，适合看书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān wūzi guāngxiàn hěn hǎo, shìhé kànshū.
examples.english: This room has good light and is perfect for reading.

examples.hanzi: 阳光的光线穿过树叶洒在地上。
examples.pinyin: Yángguāng de guāngxiàn chuānguò shùyè sǎ zài dìshàng.
examples.english: Rays of sunlight pass through the leaves onto the ground.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).
疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 疼; 痕 is the scar a sore leaves.
艮 (gèn) — near sound — 痕 is hén; 艮 also sounds out 根 gēn and 很 hěn.

example.hanzi: 他手臂上留下了一道很深的伤痕。
example.pinyin: tā shǒubì shàng liúxiàle yī dào hěn shēn de shānghén.
example.english: A deep scar was left on his arm.
example.fact: Scar tissue forms when the skin's collagen fibers rebuild in a hurried, aligned pattern rather than the random crisscross weave of normal skin, which is why scars typically lack hair follicles and sweat glands and never fully blend back into the surrounding skin.

examples.hanzi: 岁月在她的脸上留下了伤痕。
examples.pinyin: Suìyuè zài tā de liǎn shàng liúxià le shānghén.
examples.english: The years have left marks on her face.

examples.hanzi: 这次分手在他心里留下了很深的伤痕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì fēnshǒu zài tā xīn lǐ liúxià le hěn shēn de shānghén.
examples.english: The breakup left deep scars in his heart.
